speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have sudden-onset vertigo; to narrow this down, have you noticed any severe headache, double vision, or difficulty speaking alongside the spinning sensation? Also, when did these symptoms first begin, and have they been constant or coming in waves?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: That brief duration of 3 minutes is very concerning for a transient ischemic attack (TIA) or a vascular vertigo event, given your age. Have you noticed any numbness, weakness, or trouble walking after the spinning stopped? Also, do you have any history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or smoking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Circulation TIA (Transient Ischemic Attack) due to Vertebrobasilar Insufficiency. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with diffusion-weighted imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: CTA Head and Neck.
